_how_to_edit: One question per {...}. 'question': the text. 'answers': exactly 4. 'correct': the position of the right answer (0 = first, 1 = second, 2 = third, 3 = fourth). Optional 'explanation' (shown after answering) and 'image' (an https:// link, or a file name inside the images/ folder). Answers are shuffled when shown. The bot re-reads this file automatically. After editing, run: python check_trivia.py

questions.question: What does "LLM" stand for?
questions.explanation: LLMs like the ones behind chatbots are trained on huge amounts of text to predict and generate language.

questions.question: In AI agents, what is a "tool call"?
answers: The model asking the app to run an outside function or API
A phone call made by the AI
questions.explanation: Agents become useful by calling tools: search, calculators, databases, other APIs.

questions.question: What is a "multi-agent system"?
answers: Several AI agents working together on a task
questions.explanation: For example, one agent plans, another researches and another checks the work.

questions.question: What does "RAG" mean in AI?
questions.explanation: RAG looks up relevant documents first, then lets the model answer using them.

questions.question: When an AI "hallucinates", it...
answers: States something false as if it were true
questions.explanation: That's why good AI systems check facts against trusted sources.

questions.question: The Transformer architecture behind modern LLMs was introduced in which 2017 paper?
questions.explanation: Written by researchers at Google, it introduced the attention-based Transformer.

questions.question: For a language model, what is a "token"?
answers: A small chunk of text the model reads and writes
A crypto coin the model mines
questions.explanation: A token is often a word or part of a word. Models have limits measured in tokens.

questions.question: What is a model's "context window"?
answers: The maximum amount of text it can consider at once
The app window it runs in
The time of day it works best
The list of languages it speaks
questions.explanation: Anything beyond the context window is invisible to the model in that moment.

questions.question: What does "fine-tuning" a model mean?
answers: Training a pretrained model further on specific data
Running it on a faster computer
questions.explanation: Fine-tuning adapts a general model to a specific task or style.

questions.question: What is "prompt injection"?
answers: Hidden instructions in input that try to hijack an AI's behavior
A faster way to type prompts
Adding more GPUs to a server
questions.explanation: It's a key security risk for AI agents that read web pages, emails or messages.

questions.question: Since "The Merge" in 2022, which consensus mechanism does Ethereum use?
questions.explanation: Validators stake ETH instead of miners using energy-hungry hardware.

questions.question: What is a "smart contract"?
answers: A program on a blockchain that runs automatically when its conditions are met
A legal contract signed with a smart pen
A phone plan for crypto users
questions.explanation: Once deployed, its code runs exactly as written, which is why audits matter.

questions.question: What does "DAO" stand for?
questions.explanation: DAOs let members vote on decisions, often using tokens.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of bitcoins that will ever exist?
questions.explanation: The 21 million cap is built into Bitcoin's rules.

questions.question: Who published the Bitcoin whitepaper in 2008?
questions.explanation: Satoshi Nakamoto is a pseudonym. Their real identity is still unknown.

questions.question: What does "NFT" stand for?
questions.explanation: Non-fungible means each token is unique and not interchangeable with another.

questions.question: On Ethereum, what is a "gas fee"?
answers: A fee paid to process a transaction or run a smart contract
The price of fuel for mining rigs
A fee for creating an email
questions.explanation: Gas measures the computation a transaction needs.

questions.question: What is a wallet "seed phrase"?
answers: A list of words that can restore a crypto wallet
A promo code for free tokens
questions.explanation: Anyone with your seed phrase controls your funds. Never share it, not even with "support".

questions.question: What is a "Layer 2" in blockchain?
answers: A network built on top of a main chain to make transactions faster and cheaper
A backup copy of a wallet
questions.explanation: Rollups are a popular kind of Layer 2.

questions.question: What does "DeFi" stand for?
questions.explanation: DeFi apps offer lending, trading and more using smart contracts instead of banks.

questions.question: What is a "stablecoin"?
answers: A token designed to keep a steady value, often pegged to the US dollar
A coin that never moves between wallets
A coin that can only be mined in stables
questions.explanation: Stability isn't guaranteed: it depends on how the stablecoin is backed.

questions.question: In crypto, what is a "rug pull"?
answers: When a project's creators run off with investors' money
A way to clean your hardware wallet
questions.explanation: Anonymous teams, unaudited contracts and heavy hype are common warning signs.

questions.question: What do Bitcoin miners do?
answers: Compete to add new blocks by solving computational puzzles
questions.explanation: This is called Proof of Work. Miners earn new bitcoin and fees as a reward.

questions.question: What does "HODL" mean in crypto slang?
answers: Holding on to crypto instead of selling
questions.explanation: It started as a typo of "hold" in a 2013 forum post and became a meme.

questions.question: Which programming language is most commonly used for Ethereum smart contracts?
questions.explanation: Solidity was designed specifically for the Ethereum Virtual Machine.

questions.question: What is a blockchain "oracle"?
answers: A service that brings outside data, like prices, onto the blockchain
A fortune teller who predicts prices
The first miner on a network
A wallet with a huge balance
questions.explanation: Smart contracts can't read the internet by themselves, so oracles feed them data.

questions.question: Which IBM computer beat world chess champion Garry Kasparov in a 1997 match?
questions.explanation: Deep Blue's 1997 win was the first time a computer beat a reigning world champion in a match.

questions.question: In 2016, DeepMind's AlphaGo beat a top human champion at which board game?
questions.explanation: Go was long thought too complex for computers to master so soon.

questions.question: Which Go champion did AlphaGo defeat in a famous 2016 match in Seoul?
questions.explanation: AlphaGo won the five-game match 4 to 1.

questions.question: Which company's research lab created AlphaGo?
questions.explanation: DeepMind, owned by Google, built AlphaGo and later AlphaFold.

questions.question: In 2011, IBM's Watson computer beat human champions on which TV quiz show?
questions.explanation: Watson beat two of the show's greatest champions.

questions.question: DeepMind's AlphaFold is famous for predicting what?
questions.explanation: Knowing a protein's shape helps scientists understand diseases and design medicines.

questions.question: Who proposed a famous test of whether a machine can pass as a human in conversation?
questions.explanation: It's now known as the Turing test.

questions.question: What did Alan Turing originally call the test now named after him?
questions.explanation: He described it in his 1950 paper "Computing Machinery and Intelligence".

questions.question: The term "artificial intelligence" is linked to a famous 1956 summer workshop at which US college?
questions.explanation: The Dartmouth workshop is often called the birth of AI as a field.

questions.question: ELIZA, created at MIT in the 1960s, was an early example of what?
questions.explanation: ELIZA imitated a therapist by turning your words back into questions.

questions.question: What does CAPTCHA try to check?
answers: That the user is a human, not a bot
questions.explanation: CAPTCHA stands for a "Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart".

questions.question: The perceptron, invented in the 1950s, was an early type of what?
questions.explanation: It was a single artificial neuron that could learn simple patterns.

questions.question: What does "ML" stand for in tech?
questions.explanation: Machine learning lets computers learn patterns from data instead of following hand-written rules.

questions.question: In "supervised learning", what does the model learn from?
answers: Its own guesses with no feedback
questions.explanation: For example, photos already labeled "cat" or "dog".

questions.question: What does "unsupervised learning" do?
answers: Learns only from a teacher's answers
Finds patterns in data that has no labels
Trains while nobody is watching the screen
questions.explanation: Grouping customers by similar habits is a classic example.

questions.question: How does "reinforcement learning" work?
answers: It copies a textbook word for word
An agent learns by trial and error using rewards
It deletes wrong answers from the internet
questions.explanation: Good actions earn rewards, so the agent learns to repeat them.

questions.question: What is "training data"?
answers: The cost of running a model
The examples used to teach an AI model
questions.explanation: The quality of the training data strongly shapes how good the model is.

questions.question: What is "overfitting" in machine learning?
answers: Memorizing training data and doing badly on new data
questions.explanation: A good model learns general patterns, not just the examples it saw.

questions.question: Artificial neural networks were loosely inspired by what?
questions.explanation: They use connected "neurons" that pass signals to each other.

questions.question: What makes "deep learning" deep?
questions.explanation: Each layer learns more complex features than the one before.

questions.question: Which type of computer chip is widely used to train AI models?
questions.explanation: GPUs do many calculations in parallel, which suits neural networks.

questions.question: In a neural network, what are "weights" or "parameters"?
answers: Numbers the model adjusts while learning
questions.explanation: Training is mostly the process of tuning these numbers.

questions.question: Why do we keep a separate "test set" of data?
answers: To check how the model does on examples it never saw
To pay for the computer time
questions.explanation: It shows whether the model really learned or just memorized.

questions.question: Predicting a number, like tomorrow's temperature, is called what kind of ML task?
questions.explanation: Classification picks a category, regression predicts a number.

questions.question: Sorting emails into "spam" or "not spam" is an example of what?
questions.explanation: The model picks one of a fixed set of categories.

questions.question: What does "NLP" stand for in AI?
questions.explanation: NLP is about computers understanding and generating human language.

questions.question: What is "computer vision"?
answers: AI that understands images and video
questions.explanation: Face unlock and reading road signs are computer vision tasks.

questions.question: What is "generative AI"?
answers: AI that creates new content like text, images or music
AI that can only answer yes or no
questions.explanation: Chatbots and image generators are both generative AI.

questions.question: What does "GPT" stand for?
questions.explanation: It describes a model that generates text, is pretrained, and uses the Transformer design.

questions.question: In AI, what is a "prompt"?
answers: The instruction or text you give the model
The price of using the model
questions.explanation: Clearer prompts usually get better answers.

questions.question: What is "prompt engineering"?
answers: Writing and refining prompts to get better results
questions.explanation: Being specific and giving context are core prompt tips.

questions.question: What is a "system prompt"?
answers: Background instructions that set how the AI behaves in a chat
An error from the operating system
A prompt only robots can read
questions.explanation: Apps use it to give the AI a role, rules and tone.

questions.question: What is "few-shot prompting"?
answers: Limiting the model to a few answers per day
Giving the model a few examples in the prompt
Training a model on a few photos
questions.explanation: Examples show the model the exact pattern you want.

questions.question: What is "chain-of-thought" prompting?
answers: Linking several chatbots with a chain
Sending the same prompt many times
Asking the model to reason step by step
questions.explanation: Working step by step often helps with maths and logic.

questions.question: What does a higher "temperature" setting usually do to an LLM's output?
answers: Makes it always give the same answer
Makes it more random and creative
Makes it answer in capital letters
questions.explanation: Lower temperature gives more focused, predictable answers.

questions.question: In AI, what is "inference"?
answers: Using a trained model to produce answers
questions.explanation: Training teaches the model; inference is when you actually use it.

questions.question: In AI, what is an "embedding"?
answers: A video inside a web page
A list of numbers that represents the meaning of something
questions.explanation: Texts with similar meanings get similar embeddings.

questions.question: What is "pretraining" for an LLM?
answers: Testing a model before buying a GPU
The first big training run on a huge amount of text
questions.explanation: Fine-tuning and other steps usually come after pretraining.

questions.question: What does "RLHF" stand for?
questions.explanation: People rate answers, and the model learns which ones are preferred.

questions.question: What does the "large" in Large Language Model mostly refer to?
answers: The size of the computer case
The font size of its answers
Its huge number of parameters and training data
questions.explanation: Modern LLMs have billions of parameters.

questions.question: What is an "AI agent"?
answers: An AI that can take actions toward a goal, often using tools
A secret agent made of metal
A person who sells AI software
questions.explanation: Agents plan steps, use tools and check results to finish tasks.

questions.question: What does "human in the loop" mean for AI systems?
answers: A person reviews or approves the AI's important actions
A human trapped in a computer
The AI runs in an endless loop
A person types every answer manually
questions.explanation: It's a common safety practice for AI agents.

questions.question: What does "multimodal" AI mean?
answers: It runs on many computers at once
It can work with several types of data, like text and images
questions.explanation: A multimodal model might read a photo and answer questions about it.

questions.question: What is a model's "knowledge cutoff"?
answers: The maximum length of a prompt
When the model shuts down for the day
The date after which it has no training data
The point where it refuses all questions
questions.explanation: Events after the cutoff are unknown to the model unless given to it.

questions.question: What is a "deepfake"?
answers: AI-made fake video or audio of a real person
questions.explanation: Be careful: seeing or hearing something is no longer proof it's real.

questions.question: What is "bias" in AI?
answers: Unfair or skewed results, often from unbalanced training data
questions.explanation: Diverse, carefully checked data helps reduce bias.

questions.question: What does "speech recognition" do?
questions.explanation: Voice assistants and automatic captions rely on it.

questions.question: What does a "text-to-image" model do?
answers: Creates pictures from a written description
questions.explanation: You type "a cat in a spacesuit" and it draws one.

questions.question: Many popular image generators are "diffusion models". How do they create images?
answers: By copying a random photo from the web
By removing noise step by step from a random image
By drawing with a robot arm
questions.explanation: They start from static and gradually turn it into a picture.

questions.question: What is "sentiment analysis"?
answers: Counting how many words are in a text
Detecting whether text is positive, negative or neutral
questions.explanation: Companies use it to understand reviews and feedback.

questions.question: Streaming apps suggesting shows you might like use what kind of AI system?
questions.explanation: It learns from what you and similar users watch.

questions.question: What does "AGI" stand for?
questions.explanation: AGI means AI that could handle most intellectual tasks a human can.

questions.question: In AI, what are "guardrails"?
answers: Metal rails around a data center
Rules and checks that keep an AI's behavior safe
questions.explanation: They help block harmful or off-topic outputs.

questions.question: In the Transformer architecture, what does "attention" help the model do?
answers: Focus on the most relevant words in the input
questions.explanation: Attention lets each word look at the other words around it.

questions.question: What is a blockchain?
answers: A shared digital record of transactions grouped into linked blocks
A chain used to lock computers
A type of cloud storage folder
A social media app for crypto
questions.explanation: Every block points to the one before it, forming a chain.

questions.question: How is each block in a blockchain linked to the one before it?
answers: It's stored in the same folder
It has the same number of transactions
It contains the previous block's hash
questions.explanation: Changing an old block would break every link after it.

questions.question: In blockchain, what is a "hash"?
answers: A fixed-length digital fingerprint of data
questions.explanation: Change the data even slightly and the hash changes completely.

questions.question: What is a blockchain "node"?
answers: A knot in a network cable
A computer that keeps a copy of the blockchain and follows its rules
questions.explanation: Thousands of nodes make a network hard to shut down.

questions.question: What does "decentralized" mean for a blockchain?
answers: It's run by one central bank
No single company or person controls it
It only works in one country
questions.explanation: Control is spread across many participants.

questions.question: What is the very first block of a blockchain called?
questions.explanation: Bitcoin's genesis block was mined in January 2009.

questions.question: In which year was Bitcoin's first block mined?
questions.explanation: The network went live in January 2009, a few months after the whitepaper.

questions.question: What is the title of the 2008 Bitcoin whitepaper?
answers: Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System
questions.explanation: It's only nine pages long and is free to read online.

questions.question: What is the smallest unit of a bitcoin called?
questions.explanation: It's named after Bitcoin's pseudonymous creator.

questions.question: How many satoshis make one bitcoin?
questions.explanation: One satoshi is 0.00000001 BTC.

questions.question: What happens during a Bitcoin "halving"?
answers: The reward for mining a new block is cut in half
Half of all bitcoins are deleted
The price is cut in half
Transaction fees are cut in half by law
questions.explanation: Halvings happen every 210,000 blocks, roughly every four years.

questions.question: About how long does it take on average to add a new block to Bitcoin?
questions.explanation: The network adjusts mining difficulty to keep this pace.

questions.question: In 2010, a programmer famously paid 10,000 bitcoins for what?
questions.explanation: May 22 is celebrated as Bitcoin Pizza Day.

questions.question: Which consensus mechanism does Bitcoin use?
questions.explanation: Miners use computing power to secure the network.

questions.question: What is the Lightning Network?
answers: A Layer 2 for fast, cheap Bitcoin payments
A new coin that replaced Bitcoin
questions.explanation: Payments happen off-chain and settle on Bitcoin later.

questions.question: Who proposed Ethereum?
questions.explanation: He described Ethereum in a whitepaper in late 2013.

questions.question: In which year did the Ethereum network launch?
questions.explanation: Ethereum's first live release went online in July 2015.

questions.question: What is the native coin of the Ethereum network called?
questions.explanation: Its ticker is ETH, and it's used to pay gas fees.

questions.question: What is the smallest unit of Ether called?
questions.explanation: One ether equals 10^18 wei.

questions.question: Ethereum gas prices are usually quoted in which unit?
questions.explanation: One gwei is one billion wei.

questions.question: What does "EVM" stand for?
questions.explanation: The EVM runs smart contract code on every Ethereum node.

questions.question: Ethereum addresses usually start with which two characters?
questions.explanation: "0x" just means the rest is written in hexadecimal.

questions.question: What is ENS?
answers: Ethereum Name Service, which gives addresses readable names like name.eth
questions.explanation: It works a bit like domain names for wallets.

questions.question: Ethereum's switch to Proof of Stake cut its energy use by roughly how much?
questions.explanation: Validators replaced energy-hungry mining hardware.

questions.question: Why can Ethereum gas fees rise suddenly?
answers: More people want to use the network at the same time
questions.explanation: Fees work like an auction for limited block space.

questions.question: If an Ethereum transaction fails, what usually happens to the gas fee?
answers: It is still paid for the work done
It is always refunded in full
It is doubled as a penalty
It is sent to your seed phrase
questions.explanation: Validators still did the computation, so gas is used.

questions.question: What is a crypto "wallet"?
answers: A leather wallet with a chip
A bank account at a crypto bank
A tool that stores your keys and lets you manage your crypto
questions.explanation: Your coins live on the blockchain; the wallet holds the keys to them.

questions.question: Which of these is safe to share so someone can send you crypto?
questions.explanation: Your address is like an account number; keys are like the vault combination.

questions.question: What is a "private key"?
answers: A key to a crypto office
A secret code that proves you own and control your crypto
questions.explanation: Anyone who has your private key can move your funds.

questions.question: A seed phrase usually has how many words?
questions.explanation: Write the words down in the exact order shown.

questions.question: What is the safest way to store your seed phrase?
answers: As a screenshot in your photos
Offline, written on paper or metal in a safe place
In a Discord message to yourself
questions.explanation: Anything online can be hacked or leaked.

questions.question: Someone in your DMs says they're "support" and asks for your seed phrase. What should you do?
answers: Share it so they can fix your wallet
Never share it: it's a scam
questions.explanation: Real support teams will never ask for your seed phrase.

questions.question: What is a "hardware wallet"?
answers: A wallet made of metal coins
A physical device that keeps your keys offline
questions.explanation: Transactions are signed on the device, so keys never touch your computer.

questions.question: What does "Not your keys, not your coins" mean?
answers: Lost keys can be reset by email
If someone else holds your keys, you don't fully control the crypto
Coins without keys are free to take
You need physical keys to open a wallet
questions.explanation: It's a reminder of the risk of leaving funds on a platform.

questions.question: What is a "custodial" wallet?
answers: One you protect with a guard dog
One where a company holds the keys for you
One with no keys at all
questions.explanation: With non-custodial wallets, you hold the keys yourself.

questions.question: If you lose your seed phrase and your device breaks, what usually happens?
answers: The blockchain emails you a new one
The coins move to a backup bank
You can lose access to your crypto for good
questions.explanation: There's no "forgot password" button on a blockchain.

questions.question: What is "phishing"?
answers: A way to speed up transactions
Tricking people with fake sites or messages to steal their info
questions.explanation: Always check the URL before connecting your wallet.

questions.question: A stranger sends you a link to claim a "free NFT". What is the safest move?
answers: Connect fast before it runs out
Share your seed phrase to verify
Don't connect your wallet to unknown sites
Forward it to all your friends
questions.explanation: Fake mint and claim pages are a common way to drain wallets.

questions.question: A project promises "guaranteed" huge returns with no risk. This is most likely...
questions.explanation: No real investment can guarantee big returns without risk.

questions.question: Before sending crypto, what should you double-check?
answers: The recipient address and the network
The colour of the wallet app
questions.explanation: Mistakes are usually permanent.

questions.question: Can a confirmed blockchain transaction usually be reversed?
answers: Yes, by any miner on request
questions.explanation: That's why careful checking before sending matters so much.

questions.question: What is a token "approval" in a wallet?
answers: Permission for a smart contract to spend some of your tokens
questions.explanation: Revoke approvals you no longer need to reduce risk.

questions.question: Which is a good extra security step for crypto exchange accounts?
answers: Post your login on social media
questions.explanation: An authenticator app adds a strong second layer of protection.

questions.question: What is a "smart contract audit"?
answers: A security review of the contract's code
A tax check on your wallet
questions.explanation: Audits reduce risk, but they don't guarantee code is bug-free.

questions.question: Are transactions on public blockchains like Bitcoin visible to anyone?
answers: Only the sender can view them
questions.explanation: Addresses are pseudonymous, but the history is public.

questions.question: What is a "block explorer"?
answers: A website to look up blocks, transactions and addresses
A miner that finds new coins
questions.explanation: Paste a transaction hash to see its status.

questions.question: What does it mean when a transaction gets a "confirmation"?
answers: It has been included in a block
questions.explanation: More confirmations make it even harder to undo.

questions.question: What does "immutable" mean for blockchain data?
answers: It can be edited by anyone
Once recorded, it's practically impossible to change
questions.explanation: That's what makes blockchains trustworthy records.

questions.question: What is a "consensus mechanism"?
answers: A way to choose a coin's logo
The way a blockchain's nodes agree on which transactions are valid
questions.explanation: Proof of Work and Proof of Stake are the best-known examples.

questions.question: In Proof of Stake, who adds new blocks?
questions.explanation: Validators put their coins at stake to be trusted with the job.

questions.question: What does "staking" mean?
answers: Hammering a wallet into the ground
Locking up coins to help secure a network, often for rewards
questions.explanation: Staked coins can often be lost or penalized if rules are broken.

questions.question: In Proof of Stake, what is "slashing"?
answers: A penalty that takes stake from a validator who breaks the rules
questions.explanation: It gives validators a strong reason to behave honestly.

questions.question: What does "fungible" mean?
answers: Interchangeable, like one dollar for another
questions.explanation: NFTs are non-fungible: each one is unique.

questions.question: ERC-20 is a common Ethereum standard for what?
questions.explanation: Following a standard makes tokens work with many wallets and apps.

questions.question: ERC-721 is a common Ethereum standard for what?
questions.explanation: Each ERC-721 token has its own unique ID.

questions.question: What does it mean to "mint" an NFT?
answers: Create it and record it on the blockchain
questions.explanation: Minting usually costs a gas fee.

questions.question: What does it mean to "burn" tokens?
answers: Set fire to a hardware wallet
Send them to an address no one can use, removing them for good
questions.explanation: Burning reduces the amount of a token in circulation.

questions.question: What is an "airdrop" in crypto?
answers: Tokens sent to many wallets for free
A wallet backup in the cloud
questions.explanation: Be careful: fake airdrops are a common scam.

questions.question: What is a "governance token"?
answers: A token issued by a government
A token that can't be traded
A token that lets holders vote on a project's decisions
questions.explanation: DAOs often use governance tokens for voting.

questions.question: What is a "multisig" wallet?
answers: A wallet for many coins only
A wallet that needs several signatures to approve a transaction
A wallet signed by a celebrity
questions.explanation: Teams and DAOs use multisigs so no single person controls the funds.

questions.question: What does "DEX" stand for?
questions.explanation: A DEX lets people trade directly from their wallets using smart contracts.

questions.question: What is a "liquidity pool"?
answers: Tokens locked in a smart contract so people can trade them
A savings account at a bank
questions.explanation: Liquidity providers earn a share of trading fees.

questions.question: What does "AMM" stand for in DeFi?
questions.explanation: AMMs set prices with a formula instead of an order book.

questions.question: In blockchain, what is a "bridge"?
answers: A tool that moves assets between different blockchains
questions.explanation: Bridges are useful but have been a common target for hackers.

questions.question: What do "rollups" do?
answers: Bundle many transactions and post them to the main chain
questions.explanation: Sharing costs across many transactions makes each one cheaper.

questions.question: What is a "testnet"?
answers: A faster version of the main network
A practice network where tokens have no real value
questions.explanation: Developers try out apps on testnets before going live.

questions.question: What is a "dApp"?
answers: A decentralized application that runs on a blockchain
questions.explanation: dApps use smart contracts instead of a central server for key logic.

questions.question: What does "Web3" usually refer to?
answers: The third version of a website
An internet built on blockchains where users can own their assets
questions.explanation: Web1 was mostly reading, Web2 added sharing, Web3 adds ownership.

questions.question: In crypto slang, what is a "whale"?
answers: Someone who holds a very large amount of a coin
questions.explanation: Big trades by whales can move prices.

questions.question: What does "FOMO" stand for?
questions.explanation: FOMO can push people into rushed decisions.

questions.question: What does "DYOR" stand for?
questions.explanation: Always check facts yourself before trusting a project.
